title: Add missing multi-project production signals and metric dictionary
goal:
# WP2 -- Add the missing production signals (AUDIT H-5)
Audit ref: docs/tasks/5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/AUDIT.md (H-5 unmeasured behaviour); package spec: docs/tasks/5fdea223-6b10-460e-8ae7-388526798085/DELIVERABLES.md WP2. Feeds WP5 SLO gate; blocks WP5.

## Why
Multi-project behaviour is currently unmeasurable: no dispatch-latency percentiles, no per-project throughput/fairness counters, no claim-fencing rejection breakdown. Without these the WP5 SLO gate cannot pass or fail honestly, and noisy-neighbour/fairness claims (H-2) stay anecdotal. This is additive instrumentation, no behaviour change, and parallelisable with WP1.

## Required knowledge
- Files: `api/watch/observabilityMetrics.js` (existing queueDepth, scheduler stats, git contention); ledger `staleRejected` counters; `/runners/monitor` live-hold source; dispatch path `api/flow/dispatch/scanClaimableTasks.js`, `api/flow/scheduler/centralQueuePolicy.js` (`sortCentralQueue`); fleet cap `429 FLEET_CONCURRENCY_EXHAUSTED` and per-project `PROJECT_BUSY` skip paths (hook new counters here).
- Frameworks: SRE Ch.10 / OTel + RED/USE + golden signals (FRAMEWORKS section 3.8); minimum set: dispatch latency, queue depth, claim-fencing rejections, per-project throughput/fairness, worktree evictions, skill size-cap omissions.

## Do
1. Add counters/histograms: dispatch-latency p50/p95/p99; per-project claimed/completed throughput + wait-time (feeds fairness); claim success rate (non-conflict claims/attempts, excluding operator pauses and version refusals); scope/fencing rejection breakdown (PROJECT_SCOPE, STALE_EPOCH, CLAIM_CONFLICT).
2. Label per-project and queryable over a load window; extend the existing exposition, do NOT add a second metrics system.
3. Unit/integration tests on synthetic fixtures: each signal moves under a scripted scenario (burst -> fairness counters diverge correctly; conflict -> conflict counter increments).
4. Write a one-page metric dictionary (name, labels, what proves what) -- feeds WP7 runbook.

## Acceptance
- Every FRAMEWORKS section 3.8 minimum signal exists and is observable during a scripted synthetic burst; AUDIT Q8 unmeasured list for these is empty.
- Contamination check clean (no live-project writes).
> Global constraint (AUDIT section 6, DELIVERABLES header): NO real projects. All verification uses ephemeral temp-dir fixtures (proj-alpha/proj-beta style) behind api/testSetup.isolation.js + api/isolatedTestRoots.js, with before/after contamination checks on ~/projects, ~/.kainbain/projects.json, ~/.kainbain/engine/*. Live dummy projects are read-only evidence, never mutation targets. Path note: AUDIT cites /home/server2/... but relative paths (api/..., runner/..., frontend/...) are identical in this checkout.

25|in `runnerRoutes.js`, embedded tick in `scheduleTick.js`) plus progress/finish/
26|heartbeat stale-epoch sites, the 429 fleet-cap and `PROJECT_BUSY` skip paths.
27|
28|## Plan compliance — yes
29|Every IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN phase traces: counter home on `store.productionSignals`
30|(+ storeless process totals merged at exposition, the only shape that works for

40|no attempt is recorded — correct separation, not a bug.

1|# WP2 upgrade-safety audit — will existing installs break on update?
2|
3|Scope: the WP2 change on `kb/1f8959ca-265a-4f85-bb3a-c82eaa612e27` (`git diff main...HEAD`:
4|`api/watch/productionSignals.js` new, plus additive `record*` call sites and
5|`computeObservabilityMetrics` extension). Question: does updating an existing
6|install (backend restart, `docker compose` rebuild, runner self-update) break?
7|
8|Verdict: **No breakage found.** The change is additive in-memory instrumentation
9|with no migration, no new dependency, no protocol bump, and no persisted-state
10|write. Two non-breaking gaps are noted at the end (they limit the feature, they
11|do not break an update).
12|
13|## 1. Dependencies / engines / lockfiles — unchanged
14|
15|- `git diff main...HEAD -- package.json package-lock.json api/package.json
16|  api/package-lock.json runner/version.json shared/` is empty. No new npm
17|  dependency, no engine bump, no pruned-lock churn.
18|- `api/watch/productionSignals.js` has **zero imports** (`grep -c "^import"` = 0,
19|  verified). It cannot create a circular import, and the runner importing it
20|  (`runner/daemon.js`, `runner/project.js`) needs no bundled npm closure.
21|  `RUNNER_LEG_BUNDLED_DEPS` in `scripts/package-runner.mjs` stays
22|  `['@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent']` only; no change required.
23|
24|## 2. Persisted state — no migration, no file writes
25|
26|- All WP2 state lives on `taskStore.productionSignals` (lazy-attached) plus the
27|  storeless in-process totals in `productionSignals.js`. **Nothing is written to
28|  disk**: `grep writeFile/persist api/watch/productionSignals.js` is empty, and
29|  the module never touches `task.md`, `~/.kainbain/engine/*`,
30|  `~/.kainbain/projects.json`, or the runner-registry state file.
31|- A backend restart therefore resets counters to zero (the dictionary documents
32|  the counters as cumulative since `productionSignals.since`, rates = deltas of
33|  successive snapshots). Existing task/engine data is read, never rewritten.
34|- `RUNNER_STATE_VERSION` and every `task.md` shape are untouched, so an old
35|  install's files load identically after the update.
36|
37|## 3. Runner protocol — still `v1`, `facts.signals` is additive both ways
38|
39|- `RUNNER_PROTOCOL` stays `"v1"` (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`), no `MIN` bump.
40|  `runner/version.json` keeps `runnerVersion 0.1.0` with `requires.backendApi
41|  ">=1.0.0 <2.0.0"`. No handshake change.
42|- **Old runner → new backend:** `recordRunnerSignalReport(store, id,
43|  facts.signals)` returns `false` and touches nothing when `signals` is
44|  `undefined`, so a pre-WP2 daemon heartbeats with 200 and the exposition just
45|  stays at zero evictions (see `api/watch/productionSignals.js` and the
46|  `runnerRoutes.test.js` case for a heartbeat without `facts.signals`).
47|- **New runner → old backend:** `normalizeCapabilities()` reads only known
48|  keys and returns a normalized object; `record.facts` is stored raw
49|  (`runnerRegistry.js:714,1040`). The extra `facts.signals` key is inert
50|  advisory data on an old backend that never reads it — heartbeat/register
51|  still validate the same fields and cannot 400 on the new key (the same
52|  additive-field rule `sanitizeVersions` documents for `values.build`).
53|- The `signals` payload itself is capped to one finite counter
54|  (`worktreeEvictions`), monotone-merged per runner, so a restarted runner can
55|  never move the fleet total backwards.
56|
57|## 4. Shipping — the new file reaches every install path
58|
59|- Backend/docker: `Dockerfile` does `COPY api/ ./api/` and `deploy.sh --prod`
60|  stages `tar -C api ...` wholesale, so `api/watch/productionSignals.js` ships
61|  (see `deploy.sh:1723`). No file is deleted or renamed.
62|- Runner distributable: `scripts/package-runner.mjs` `copyPruned(root/api → stage/api)`
63|  for `scripts/package-runner.sh` and `deploy.sh:1723-1724`, so the daemon that
64|  imports `../api/watch/productionSignals.js` resolves in the bundled runner
65|  tree. Wrapper installs (`runner-install-root.sh`) lay down `runner + api +
66|  shared` wholesale (`cp -a api/.`), so an update overwrites the tree with the
67|  new module present. No stale-tree `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` window.
68|- `api/index.js:241` adds one in-memory line `taskStore.executionLedger =
69|  executionLedger`; the `ExecutionLedger` constructor signatures are unchanged.
70|
71|## 5. API surface — additive response keys only
72|
73|- `computeObservabilityMetrics` gains an optional third param `opts = {}`
74|  (`api/watch/observabilityMetrics.js:35`), so all existing callers
75|  (`taskStore.getObservabilityMetrics`, `status.js:358`,
76|  `observabilityMetrics.test.js`) keep working with no change.
77|- The response gains `queueDepthByProject`, `ledgerStaleRejected`, and
78|  `productionSignals` alongside untouched `stats.queueDepth`, `schedulerStats`,
79|  `gitContention`, `executionQueue`. Nothing is removed or renamed; no frontend
80|  file references the new keys (`grep` in `frontend/` is empty), so the UI
81|  cannot break on new fields.
82|- Instrumentation never gates dispatch: every `record*` funnels through
83|  `mutateSignals`, which swallows its own faults (frozen/locked store,
84|  malformed args drop the sample). A legacy or frozen `taskStore` therefore
85|  degrades to "no signal", never a failed dispatch. This is what makes the
86|  call-site insertions in `runnerRoutes.js`, `scheduleTick.js`, and
87|  `skillInjection.js` non-behavioural.
88|
89|## 6. Update scenarios for existing installs
90|
91|- **Backend restart with in-flight tasks:** signals are event counters, not
92|  derived state; in-flight claims/com completions are unaffected. Future
93|  failures only change where they are counted.
94|- **Runner self-update / wrapper reinstall:** the new tree contains the new
95|  module and the `facts.signals` field; an old runner that has not yet
96|  self-updated keeps working against the new backend (§3).
97|- **Mixed fleet during a rolling update:** both directions are forward- and
98|  backward-compatible per §3; no version floor change forces an upgrade.
99|- **Frozen/legacy doubles and persisted state files:** lazy attach plus
100|  try/catch means old shapes (no `productionSignals`, no `executionLedger`)
101|  yield empty-but-total summaries; `ledgerStaleRejected: null` when no ledger
102|  handle exists.
103|
104|## Non-breaking gaps (do not fail the stage)
105|
106|- `taskStore.getObservabilityMetrics(filterProjectId)` does not forward `opts`,
107|  so the HTTP `/status` observability path always reports full history; the
108|  `{ windowMs, now }` window only takes effect via direct
109|  `computeObservabilityMetrics(store, undefined, { windowMs, now })` calls
110|  (as the dictionary documents). This weakens the load-window story on the
111|  served endpoint but does not break any existing install or response.
112|- `runner/version.json` (`0.1.0`) was not bumped, so the runner self-update
113|  channel will not notice this code change by version alone (hosts keep the
114|  old daemon, which is safe per §3). A future release should bump it so
115|  eviction reporting reaches existing fleets without a manual reinstall.
116|

1|import { isLiveAccessibilityFeedbackPath } from "./isLiveAccessibilityFeedbackPath.js";
2|
3|/***
4| * MARK: throwIfLiveAccessibilityFeedbackPathUnderTest
5| * @description Test-pollution guard for the accessibility-feedback inbox
6| *   (residual D9 of 99ccc12f, task b3dec9b0): while `VITEST` is set,
7| *   resolving the LIVE `~/.kainbain/accessibility-feedback.jsonl` inbox
8| *   THROWS, so a suite that forgets its `KAINBAIN_ACCESSIBILITY_FEEDBACK_FILE`
9| *   temp override fails loudly in CI instead of silently appending test
10| *   reports to the real user inbox (survey q1: throw, not silent redirect).
11| *   A no-op when `VITEST` is unset (production resolves byte-identically)
12| *   or when the path is a temp/explicit inbox — including non-string
13| *   values, which carry no path to guard. Gate matches the engine guard
14| *   (`VITEST` only) so both guards sleep and fire together.
15| * @example throwIfLiveAccessibilityFeedbackPathUnderTest({ candidatePath: '/tmp/x.json', callerName: 'resolveFeedbackFile' }) => undefined
16| * @param {Object} args - Labelled inputs.
17| * @param {*} args.candidatePath - Resolved path to guard (anything; only the live inbox string throws).
18| * @param {string} [args.callerName] - Resolver name stamped into the error so the fix location is obvious.
19| * @returns {void}
20| ***/
21|export function throwIfLiveAccessibilityFeedbackPathUnderTest({
22|	candidatePath,
23|	callerName,
24|} = {}) {
25|	if (!process.env.VITEST) return;
26|	if (!isLiveAccessibilityFeedbackPath(candidatePath)) return;
27|	const caller =
28|		typeof callerName === "string" && callerName.trim()
29|			? callerName.trim()
30|			: "accessibility-feedback guard";
31|	throw new Error(
32|		`${caller} refused live accessibility-feedback path under test: ${candidatePath} ` +
33|			`(VITEST is set). Pin the inbox at a temp path via its ` +
34|			`KAINBAIN_ACCESSIBILITY_FEEDBACK_FILE env var (see api/testSetup.isolation.js) ` +
35|			`instead of reading or writing ~/.kainbain/accessibility-feedback.jsonl from tests.`,
36|	);
37|}

{
  "projectId": "0fd41821-d8a5-4e49-bc2e-28ce8c739a0a",
  "workflowId": "wf-default",
  "stageId": "1",
  "execute": false,
  "idempotencyKey": "0dbb6e7f3dc8afc855afc8a82b0fb91c",
  "title": "Stop canary resource-exhaustion flakes from failing the whole CI gate",
  "goal": "PROBLEM: A single Playwright canary spec failing with an infrastructure-class error (dead browser / renderer crash after a long serial run) fails the entire Automated-tests gate and triggers fallback routing, even when every fast-gate branch is green and the ticket touches no UI code. The repo policy (canary-e2e/playwright.config.js, retries: 0) keeps flakes visible so root causes get fixed, and ticket 8769b002 built a quarantine lane for known flakes -- but new infra-class flakes still land as hard gate failures with no lane and no attribution, burning a full ~29-minute CI cycle per occurrence. CASE STUDY: Kainbain task 1f8959ca-265a-4f85-bb3a-c82eaa612e27 (WP2 production signals, backend + runner instrumentation only, zero frontend files touched) failed Automated tests with all 13 fast-gate branches green and canary at 139/140; the one failure was tests/footer-overlay.spec.js dying in page.goto with 'Target page, context or browser has been closed' ~15 minutes into the serial canary phase (resource exhaustion on the shared gate host). Evidence: docs/tasks/1f8959ca-265a-4f85-bb3a-c82eaa612e27/automated-tests-failure-20261116-234841.md and ci-fast-gate-20261116-232853/canary-tests.full.log; the failure class matches the infra-error regex already recognised in canary-e2e/tests/helpers.js (ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES|has been closed|Target closed|Page crashed|Target crashed), whose single bounded re-issue also failed because the browser was gone. FIX (structural, keeps flakes visible): (1) root-cause the resource pressure behind serial-run browser death (suspect accumulated resource use across 140 serial specs on the 4-core gate host; check browser-context reuse, memory growth, and the 7.1-minute accessibility.spec.js flagged as slow in the same log); (2) route failures matching the existing infra-class regex to the quarantine/non-blocking lane from 8769b002 (visible but not gate-failing) instead of failing the whole run, and record footer-overlay as a quarantine entry with its baseline; (3) make the CI report attribute canary failures to ticket scope (backend-only diff vs UI suites touched) so agents stop hand-verifying unrelatedness. ACCEPTANCE: an infra-class canary failure on a ticket with no UI changes produces a visible, attributed, non-blocking signal (quarantine lane) instead of a FAILED gate plus fallback routing; the footer-overlay spec has a recorded quarantine entry or a proven root-cause fix; retries policy for genuine assertion failures stays at 0."
}
EOF
curl -s -m 15 -X POST http://192.168.1.206:3100/tasks -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @/tmp/kb_ticket1.json | head -c 1500","description":"Create canary flake ticket"}
